title: Distorted Face Emoji (🫪): Meaning, Codepoint & Where It Came From
meta_description: The distorted face emoji 🫪 (U+1FAEA) — its Unicode 17.0 codepoint, what it actually means, how to type it, and the real design history behind it.
hero_tagline: The stretched, inflated face 🫪 — codepoint, meaning, alt-input shortcuts, and the documented design history behind Unicode 17.0's most talked-about new emoji. Click any symbol to copy it instantly.
intro: 🫪 DISTORTED FACE (U+1FAEA) is a face pulled out of shape — swollen, stretched, and slightly airborne. Unicode added it in version 17.0 on 9 September 2025, and within months it was the new emoji people actually used, winning both "Most Popular New Emoji" and "Most '2026' Emoji" at Emojipedia's World Emoji Awards. This page identifies the glyph itself — meaning, codepoint, and how to type it — then covers where the design genuinely came from, including the widely-repeated origin story that its own Unicode proposal does not support.
